text:
Maya (CSM): Heads-up team: AnchorHaven's private deploy preflight uncovered two things we need to clear before week1: their KMS ACL blocks cross-account grants, and their egress proxy is stripping S3 signed headers. Can we hammer out fixes now?
Leo (Network Eng): Stripping signed headers means the proxy is doing TLS offload or header normalization. If they insist on proxy, the shortest path is: 1) add VPC Gateway endpoint for S3, 2) route CloudTrail traffic through the endpoint to avoid proxy entirely. Do they have route table permissions to add endpoints?
Maya (CSM): They said infra team can add endpoints, but the perimeter firewall blocks endpoint prefix lists currently.
Priya (Security): On the KMS side, the CMK policy denies principals outside their account. Their security lead wants full auditability so they insisted on using their CMK. We need a grant or key policy change. Also they asked if enabling automatic rotation would impact our ingestion.
Sam (Solutions Eng): Two workable options: create a KMS grant for our cross-account writer role (fast, scoped), or ask them to add our provisioning role to the key policy (longer-lived). For rotation: if they enable automatic rotation on the same CMK, key id stays the same and existing grants remain valid. If they create a new key and switch alias, grants must be recreated. Recommend automatic rotation on current key.
Leo (Network Eng): Firewall change list to request: allow PLs for `com.amazonaws.us-west-2.s3` and `com.amazonaws.us-west-2.kms` if they use VPC endpoints that reference KMS (rare). Also ensure route tables in the private subnets include the S3 gateway endpoint route.
Priya (Security): Bucket policy note: CloudTrail delivery requires the CloudTrail service principal plus our writer role. Example snippet to add: "Principal": {"AWS": ["arn:aws:iam::999888777666:role/redwood-delivery"], "Service": "cloudtrail.amazonaws.com"}. Also ensure the bucket policy doesn't enforce `aws:SourceIp` that blocks AWS internal IPs.
Sam (Solutions Eng): For SIEM ingestion, AnchorHaven uses a partner SIEM (LogStream) pulling objects from S3. Their IAM role for the SIEM lacks `s3:GetObjectVersion` and `s3:GetObject` on the audit prefix. We'll need them to add these permissions and to add the SIEM role as a principal in the bucket policy.
Maya (CSM): Action owners please: KMS grant/policy — Priya will own. Firewall/endpoint + routes — Leo. Bucket policy & SIEM permissions — AnchorHaven to update but Sam will validate.
Priya (Security): I'll prepare the minimal key policy snippet and a grant example. Prefer grant during cutover: CLI to create grant quickly: `aws kms create-grant --key-id <key-id> --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::555444333222:role/redwood-s3-writer --operations Encrypt GenerateDataKey`
Sam (Solutions Eng): I'll also prepare a small test harness: 1) attempt `aws s3 cp` using the cross-account role to the bucket; 2) check CloudTrail object-level PutObject events; 3) verify SIEM pickup. If bucket rejects due to signed header stripping, test will fail and we'll know it's proxy.
Leo (Network Eng): If they can't open firewall today, fallback is to provision a small NAT/Gateway for bootstrap host to allow signed PUTs. That adds cost and a short delay but is quick to stand up. Ops estimate ~2 hours to create NAT + route changes.
Maya (CSM): They prefer not to add NAT. Ingrid (customer infra) said they can push firewall rules but may need approval from compliance — could be a 4 hour window.
ops-bot: runbook created: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/CS-10821 "AnchorHaven private deploy preflight"
Priya (Security): Rotation/Renewal risk: AnchorHaven wants yearly rotation and strict audit retention. If they rotate keys by swapping alias to new key id during renewal, we need a process to re-create grants. I'll draft a small runbook step that they can include in their rotation automation to call `create-grant` for our role.
Sam (Solutions Eng): For the smoke test tomorrow morning: prerequisites — 1) KMS grant exists, 2) bucket policy updated to allow CloudTrail & our role, 3) endpoint/routes present or proxy allows PUTs, 4) SIEM role has read perms. If those are done, I'll run the put-object test and validate CloudTrail event within 10m.
Leo (Network Eng): I'll provide the exact route-table check: `aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-0dce1234 --query 'RouteTables[].Routes[]'` and a pointer to validate endpoints: `aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-0dce1234`
Maya (CSM): Timeline ask: can we get KMS grant and bucket policy changes by EOD? They said compliance might delay firewall but can do the policy changes.
Priya (Security): I'll own the key grant request template and send to Ingrid with exact CLI and console steps. If they want us to do it, we need an assume-role window.
Sam (Solutions Eng): I'll prepare a rollback checklist: 1) stop CloudTrail delivery, 2) remove temporary grants, 3) reconfigure to Redwood-managed bucket if ingest fails. Also add monitoring: if PutObject errors exceed 5 in 10m, trigger ops alert.
Maya (CSM): Great. Ingrid just replied in the customer thread: "We'll add the bucket policy at 2pm, and we'll allow the grant creation so you can run the test at 7pm PT."
Leo (Network Eng): I'll stand by to review endpoint and route table after their change.
Priya (Security): Once grant is created, I'll immediately run a `kms:GenerateDataKey` simulation from the cross-account principal to confirm permissions.
Maya (CSM): Thanks team. If firewall doesn't clear by tomorrow morning we'll postpone the dry-run to avoid false negatives. Otherwise keep the 9am slot. :ok_hand:
